title: Chromecast mixes subtitle languages and timestamps after upgrading to Jellyfin 10.9.x
body: After upgrading my Jellyfin server from 10.8.13-1 to 10.9.x, subtitles become unreadable when I cast from the Android client to a Chromecast. Playback usually starts correctly, but after a few subtitle lines, text from multiple language tracks and unrelated timestamps is overlaid or shown randomly even though I selected only one language. The same movies work correctly in a web browser and the Android web player. I confirmed the problem on 10.9.3 and 10.9.6. It is much easier to reproduce with large external SRT tracks and is strongly correlated with server log messages such as `163 errors encountered while parsing 'srt' subtitle using the SubRip format parser`. Enabling or disabling on-the-fly subtitle extraction does not change it. My server runs Debian Bookworm with jellyfin-ffmpeg6, Intel QSV, no plugins or reverse proxy.

symptoms_visible: When I cast from Android to Chromecast, playback starts with the selected subtitle language but soon shows lines from multiple languages and unrelated timestamps overlaid on each other or skips lines entirely.
The same movies and subtitle tracks display normally in a web browser and the Android web player.
The failure is much more frequent with full-size SRT files, and the server usually logs many SubRip parsing errors when it happens.
N0.label: N0 Chromecast subtitle mixing reported

symptoms_visible: The mixed and overlaid subtitles occur during Chromecast playback while the server is transcoding the video.
N1.label: N1 playback method established

symptoms_visible: After upgrading to the server release containing the libse version bump, the same media still produces the same mixed-language subtitles and parser errors.
N2_x.label: N2_x dependency-bump aftermath

symptoms_visible: The subtitle files in the cache appear to contain one language each, but playback still combines multiple tracks.
The server logs overlapping attempts to parse different subtitle files and reports matching parsing-error counts while the mixed subtitles appear.
Changing extraction settings, clearing the cache, or using the extraction plugin may reduce the frequency temporarily, but the mixing returns.
N2.label: N2 cached files and concurrent parsing examined

symptoms_visible: In a test build that obtains fresh subtitle-format objects inside each parse call, media that previously mixed subtitle tracks displays the selected subtitles correctly.
N3.label: N3 fresh parser-instance test succeeds

symptoms_visible: Another affected user reports that subtitles display correctly after updating to a build containing the parser-instance fix; I have not retested that landed build on my own Chromecast setup.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix landed with third-party confirmation

question_patterns: When this happens, does the dashboard or server log say the Chromecast session is direct playing, remuxing, or transcoding?
Can you paste the playback-method section of the log from an affected cast?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: For the example I checked, the log says `PlayMethod=Transcode`. The MKV example gives `ContainerNotSupported`; affected MP4 examples can give `VideoResolutionNotSupported`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It only happens during direct play, and I cannot reproduce it during transcoding.
It is still transcoding, but the reason is an unsupported audio format rather than the container or resolution.

edges.comment: Thread c3-c6, reporter cchristchurch: participant2 asked for the playback method and reason; the reporter pasted logs showing transcoding for both affected and unaffected examples.

solution.intent: Resolve the parser errors by updating the subtitle parsing dependency to a newer build.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade to the server release containing the newer libse package and replay the same affected media.

edges.comment: Thread c13-c18: participant5 initially reported success from changing libse versions, but reporter cchristchurch upgraded to 10.9.9 with the bump and observed identical symptoms and errors. participant5 later withdrew the earlier conclusion as inaccurate.

question_patterns: Can you inspect the extracted subtitle files in the server subtitle cache and tell me whether an individual file already contains mixed languages?
Are the cached SRT files themselves garbled, or does each file still contain only its own language?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I checked several files in the subtitle cache. They look reasonable, and each file I examined contains subtitles in only one language rather than the mixed content shown during playback.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Each cached SRT file already contains interleaved lines from several languages.
I found minor formatting errors in one file, but every cached file still contains only one language.

question_patterns: Can you compare the detailed parser log timestamps for two subtitle tracks during one failure?
What is the exact order of the charset, parse-start, and parse-error messages when the languages become mixed?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The log starts parsing the English SRT, then starts parsing the French SRT before the first call finishes. The two error messages then appear a few milliseconds apart with the same count, for example 120 errors for each parse.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every subtitle parse completes before the next one begins; there is no overlap in the timestamps.

edges.comment: Thread c9, c19, c30-c35: dpad and khellste inspected extracted files and found separate, single-language content; reporter cchristchurch supplied the interleaved parser timeline. These affected users are folded into one simulated user side without treating their different installations as one physical system. Reports in c21-c29 also establish that extraction-plugin and cache-clearing workarounds eventually fail.

question_patterns: Can you test a build that creates fresh subtitle-format objects inside each Parse call instead of reusing the startup-created objects?
Please move subtitle-format discovery into the parse method in a test build and replay media that reliably showed the issue.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I changed the Parse function to call `GetSubtitleFormats()` inside the method. All the media I tested that had shown the problem before now displays the subtitles correctly.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The modified build still mixes languages on the same media.
The modified build works on all tested media but starts playback slightly more slowly.

edges.comment: Thread c36-c40: alltilla and khellste proposed testing fresh format objects; affected user participant13 built the proof of concept and reported only the observed playback result. The conclusion that cached instances are stateful or non-thread-safe remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Stop sharing subtitle-format parser instances across concurrent parse calls: cache format types or metadata, then construct a fresh selected parser instance for every subtitle parse, and ask affected users to verify a build containing the change.
solution.concrete_example: Replace the cache of live SubtitleFormat objects with a cache of their types, instantiate the selected format inside each Parse call, and have affected Chromecast users replay previously failing multi-track media. The change was merged and one affected user reported correct subtitles after updating to the latest 10.10.5 push.
solution.inference_hint: The users supplied separate single-language cache files, overlapping parse timestamps, repeated parser errors, and a successful fresh-instance test. Concluding that the cached libse SubtitleFormat instances carry shared mutable state and are unsafe across concurrent Parse calls is the maintainer's diagnosis, not a raw user measurement.

edges.comment: Thread c40-c46: alltilla refined the proof of concept to cache format classes/types and instantiate one selected parser per call, then opened and landed the fix. normanu, a different affected user, confirmed correct behavior on the latest 10.10.5 push. Reporter cchristchurch did not return to confirm the landed release, so the terminal state records relayed confirmation and user_perceives_resolved remains false.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: live libse SubtitleFormat parser instances were cached and reused by concurrent subtitle Parse calls, allowing shared mutable parser state to mix otherwise separate subtitle tracks.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: cached SRT files contain one language each, parser executions overlap in the logs, and a test using fresh format instances per Parse displays previously affected media correctly.
The fix must create a fresh subtitle-format instance for each parse call; caching format types or metadata is acceptable, but reusing live parser instances is not.

Must not present a libse version bump, extraction toggle, Subtitle Extract plugin, or subtitle-cache reset as the resolution; each was shown to be ineffective or only temporarily helpful in this case.
Must not blame the HTML secondary-subtitle feature as the final root cause; the accepted diagnosis is concurrent reuse of stateful server-side subtitle parser instances.

Must ask an affected user to verify a build containing the parser-instance fix before declaring the user's setup resolved. The thread contains confirmation from a different affected user, but no final retest from the original reporter.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable self-hosting user who can interpret Jellyfin debug logs, compare source changes, modify subtitle files and test server releases, but is not deeply familiar with Jellyfin's architecture. Other affected users who inspect cache files or compile test changes are folded into the user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, methodical and cooperative; provides extensive logs and controlled experiments, clearly labels uncertainty, and challenges tentative diagnoses with reproducible counterevidence.
